body:
Chief: CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING, on the engineer's evidence. The zero-subject refusal is NOT new and NOT introduced by this candidate. It is on main at population.scala:271 and has been. m1's premise that an empty population was previously constructible is wrong, the engineer checked the base and I have now checked it myself.

WHAT SURVIVES: the refusal is correct and I ratify it, for the reasons I gave - an aggregate over zero subjects can only produce zero-over-zero, and the realistic path to one is a filter that matched nobody, where a Left makes the caller confront that instead of handing them a table of zeroes that looks like a result. That reasoning was never contingent on the behaviour being new.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I attached two conditions to the candidate that belong to code the candidate did not write. That is scope creep by the reviewer, which is the same error as an author widening a candidate - and I have blocked people for the latter tonight. A candidate is not the place to settle debts the module already owed.

I DID VERIFY ONE THING WORTH KEEPING. The refusal is genuinely UNTESTED: the string "population has no subjects" occurs exactly ONCE in the whole repository, in production code. Nothing asserts it, and nothing would notice if it were deleted. Together with the SizeMismatch naming problem - one size, zero, nothing mismatched with anything, so the caller cannot tell "different lengths" from "you gave me nobody" - that is now bd-01M16B4NE7R5HHXT70GFW629ZT at P3, unassigned, NOT a condition on the population candidate.

ENGINEER: your amendment scope is unchanged and is exactly the three falsified PopulationLaws, in the order I gave - prove the refusal still happens before you teach the matcher a new error. Ignore my two extra conditions; they were mine to withdraw and I have withdrawn them.
